clue.text: Bridle? Not a bit of it!

definitions.text: Bridle? Not a bit of it!

parts.words: Bridle? Not a bit of it!
parts.note: a piece of horse tack for the head that, unusually, has no mouthpiece at all

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a bit of it!' reads as a flat denial, but it literally describes a headstall that works on the nose with no bit in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: This Western-style headgear controls a horse by pressure on the nose rather than through a metal mouthpiece.

clue.text: A native American ruffian in Paris

explanation.surface: A Native American is described as a thug in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Parisian slang borrowed the tribal name for a street hoodlum in the early 1900s.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a southwestern US tribe, and also a Parisian gangster or street thug of the Belle Époque.

clue.text: Was it used by Alexander the great? Pass!

definitions.text: Was it used by Alexander the great? Pass!

parts.words: Was it used by Alexander the great? Pass!
parts.note: 'Pass!' looks like a quizzer declining to answer, but it names a mountain route Alexander's army is reputed to have taken towards India

explanation.definitionFit: A famous mountain pass between Afghanistan and Pakistan, a historic invasion route into the subcontinent.

clue.text: A bed to rest on for mum, Troy and Brian

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'A bed to rest on for mum, Troy and Brian (6)'. MATRIX fits 'A bed', but no parse of 'mum, Troy and Brian' gives the letters and a search found no other text.
annotationWithheld.clue: A bed to rest on for mum, Troy and Brian

clue.text: Communist referendum gets the bird

parts.note: a Red is a common informal word for a Communist
a referendum is a poll of the voters on one question

explanation.surface: A left-wing vote ends in a raspberry, 'getting the bird' meaning being booed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' looks like the idiom for being jeered; here 'gets' is a link and 'the bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small finch with a crimson forehead patch.

clue.text: System that's complicated for us

parts.note: something complicated is complex

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a scheme is too intricate for ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin-derived term for an interwoven network or structure, as of nerves or muscles.

clue.text: Scared of getting stoned?

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if fright comes from being high on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrified out of one's wits, and literally turned into stone as in fossilised wood.

clue.text: Derby provides a good example

parts.note: the Derby is a famous flat contest for thoroughbreds at Epsom, not the English city or a bowler hat

explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is the best-known English flat event for three-year-old thoroughbreds, run at Epsom each summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitive gallop for thoroughbreds, of which the Epsom classic is the prime instance.

clue.text: Something to wear for the dance

explanation.surface: Someone picks out an outfit for a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A short open jacket ending above the waist, and a lively Spanish dance in triple time.

clue.text: Women carrying building materials

parts.note: the women are carved stone pillars bearing the entablature of a temple on their heads

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like female labourers on a site; in fact the figures are columns sculpted as women, as on the Erechtheion in Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical architecture used sculpted female figures in place of columns to hold up a roof.

clue.text: Soccer and cricket at Southampton and newhaven, maybe

explanation.surface: Games are being played at two English south-coast towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Southampton and Newhaven are harbours on England's south coast, so they are 'S ports'.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket are games; the two towns are southern harbours, read as S plus a word for harbours.

clue.text: A piece of paper to press on metal

parts.note: a single leaf of paper is a sheet
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Someone presses a page flat against a metal surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrous metal rolled into thin flat plates.

clue.text: In French, "vache", I ferret out

indicators.note: to ferret out is to dig something up from within, so the letters lie inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A French speaker explains a farmyard word they have tracked down.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are concealed across 'vache I ferret'; vache is French for cow, which the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cow that has not yet calved, a fair rendering of the French farm animal.

clue.text: They alter commercials — right the queen should appear in them

indicators.note: these words say the following pieces are placed inside the commercials

parts.note: advertisements are ads
right as in fair is just
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: Tinkerers fix adverts so that the monarch appears in them.
explanation.definitionFit: People who modify or correct things, such as insurance claim assessors.

clue.text: Lessening beam at ten cycles

indicators.note: cycling around suggests the letters going round and changing places

explanation.surface: A light beam pulses at ten cycles per second.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction or easing, as in a tax or noise reduction.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory collectors of alms?

parts.note: 'unsatisfactory' is a sense of the adjective meaning substandard, while the containers collect for the needy

explanation.walkthrough: The clue pretends the containers are badly made; really the adjective names who the money is for.
explanation.definitionFit: Church collection containers in which donations for the needy are placed.

clue.text: Boxer — malian no man's seen

indicators.note: 'no man' means the letters of that word are taken away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fighter from Mali is seen by no one.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M, the second A and N from MALIAN, leaving the famous heavyweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was a world heavyweight boxing champion.

clue.text: He's a fool to muck around with the sas

indicators.note: mucking around with something messes it up, so the letters get jumbled

explanation.surface: Only an idiot fools about with Special Air Service soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is Britain's Special Air Service regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey, and figuratively a stupid person.

clue.text: A 3-letter alphabet? Initially, yes

parts.note: a system of phonetic symbols whose full name is usually shortened to three initials

explanation.definitionFit: The International Phonetic Alphabet, a notation for speech sounds known by its initials.

clue.text: Having doubts, calls in debt

parts.note: to dub is to call or name
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: Someone is uncertain after being asked to repay what they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling uncertain or hesitant about something.

clue.text: A composer beginning with p? No clue about this one!

definitions.text: A composer beginning with p? No clue about this one!

parts.words: A composer beginning with p? No clue about this one!
parts.note: the setter admits giving only the opening letter of a French musician's name

explanation.walkthrough: A tongue-in-cheek clue: the only help is that the composer's name starts with P.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Poulenc was a French composer, one of Les Six.

clue.text: Spelling a resort's name

parts.note: sp is the proofreader's abbreviation marking a spelling error

explanation.surface: Someone is spelling out the name of a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Belgian town of Spa gave its name to health resorts generally.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian mineral-spring town, the name of which became the word for any such resort.

clue.text: Musketeer who left host no time to finish

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

indicators.note: 'no' says a letter is to be removed
'to finish' says the removal is at the end of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A swordsman walked out on his host before the evening ended.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Dumas's three swordsmen, alongside Athos and Aramis.

clue.text: Speaks to whole society

parts.note: utter means complete or total

explanation.surface: Someone addresses the entire community.
explanation.definitionFit: Says aloud or voices words.

clue.text: Area of England, by the river, that has decayed

parts.note: SE is south-east England
the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A region of England beside a river has fallen into ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentally or physically declining through old age.

clue.text: Superior journalist, with a feather in his cap?

definitions.text: with a feather in his cap?

parts.note: plum describes something choice or excellent, as in a plum job
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A top reporter has earned an honour, a feather in his cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a feather in his cap' is an idiom for an achievement, here taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorated with feathers, as a hat bearing a plume.

clue.text: 2 = one

parts.note: the answer to clue 2 names a tribe, and a member of it is one of the continent's native peoples

explanation.walkthrough: Clue 2 is APACHE: an Apache is a Native American, once called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: An Apache is one of the indigenous peoples of the Americas, traditionally termed this.

clue.text: Finds Lear being played in Holland

indicators.note: a play being staged changes, so the letters are acted out in a new order

explanation.surface: A Dutch audience discovers Shakespeare's King Lear on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern province of the Netherlands.

clue.text: An instrument for the piper's son

explanation.surface: A drum is meant for the boy in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom, Tom, the piper's son' is an English nursery rhyme about a boy who stole a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall drum beaten by hand, and the doubled name of the rhyme's pig-stealing boy.

clue.text: Annoying letters about armour?

explanation.surface: Irritating correspondence concerns battle gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Chain letters are messages the recipient is pressed to forward; linked rings form the knight's protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages one is urged to pass on to others, and protective gear of interlinked metal rings.

clue.text: Diners might have washed!

indicators.note: the phrase hints at a possible version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restaurant guests may have cleaned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might have' tells you to rearrange DINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rinsed means cleaned with water.

clue.text: Going up when clubs are closing

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs
a closing is an ending

explanation.surface: Something is rising just as nightclubs shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing or rising higher.
